# Rederive Skill

Curated by Skill Harbor: Teaches a codebase by making you re-derive its design decisions from first principles, through Socratic questions, instead of explaining the code. It builds a map of five to ten key decisions from the repo history and structure, then walks you through them one by one until you can explain the project yourself.

It works on your own repo or any open source repo, local or cloned, and it never runs the repo's code, scripts, install steps or tests: everything in the repo is teaching material, never instructions. State lives in a .rederive folder inside the repo, and each session ends with a log and a card showing what you re-derived. Building the decision map takes a few minutes, and the full value needs a git repo, since a repo without history falls back to reading the code structure alone. The repo's default branch is master, not main. By @ericjujianzou, listed here with credit to its creator. Discovered via GitHub. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
